shadow.name: --shadow-glow
shadow.raw: 0 0 200px color-mix(in srgb, var(--c2010) 30%, transparent), 0 2px 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--c2110) 30%, transparent), 0 4px 30px 10px color-mix(in srgb, var(--c2010) 15%, transparent)

components.name: Input
components.usage: Use native single-line entry with a persistent associated label. Actual value, focus, disabled/readOnly and application error determine the selected Figma states.

examples.label: Payment message
examples.code: <Input label="Mitteilung" name="message" value={message} onChange={e => setMessage(e.target.value)} maxLength={120} showCharacterCount helperText="Verwendungszweck" error={errors.message} />

antipatterns: Do not substitute a placeholder for the label or force interaction states through styling props.
Do not invent colors, automatic validation or masking; decorative affixes and icons are not actions.

components.name: Icon
components.usage: Use for the curated Raiffeisen icon vocabulary, as decorative support for a label or inside an accessible control. Icons inherit the surrounding semantic color.

examples.label: Confirmation status
examples.code: import { Icon } from '@/design-system/{slug}'; Payment confirmed

antipatterns: Do not use an icon outside the curated IconName set.
Do not use an icon-only control without an accessible parent label.
Do not use arbitrary icon sizes or hardcoded colors.

components.name: Button
components.usage: Use Primary for the main action, Secondary for supporting negative actions, and Link for less prominent actions. Set href for navigation and isLoading for non-blocking local processing.
antipatterns: Never use Primary on black or red backgrounds; use inverted Secondary or Link.
Do not use Secondary alone for a positive action.
Do not use isLoading for blocking processes or on red backgrounds.
Do not replace the application live-region progress and result feedback with a loading button.

components.name: Logo
components.usage: Use the verbatim Raiffeisen wordmark to identify the brand in headers, footers and sign-in screens. Two token-backed heights; named for assistive technology unless decorative next to text that already names the brand.
antipatterns: Do not recolor, stretch, crop or redraw the wordmark, and do not recreate it with text or a generated image.
Do not place it on colored or inverted surfaces or use it as a loading indicator or inside buttons.

components.name: LoaderSquare
components.usage: Use small for elements or large for empty pages without a skeleton. Animated neutral loaders loop between static and reference shapes with system motion tokens; Button loading composes the animated small neutral loader with a reduced-motion static fallback.
antipatterns: Do not add a loader where a skeleton already represents the same pending content.
Do not introduce custom timings, animate Brand or override reduced-motion preferences.
Do not replace application-owned busy state and announcements with this decorative loader.

components.name: Badge
components.usage: Use counter (default) for non-negative counts, capped at 99+, or dot for the selected numberless new/unread indicator. Both work alone or in Button's badge slot. Provide accessible count or indicator context.
antipatterns: Do not make Badge an interactive control or nest actions inside it.
Do not invent colors or variants beyond counter and dot.
Do not use badge typography as a general text style.
Do not communicate the dot's meaning by color alone; add accessible context.

components.name: Skeleton
components.usage: Use static neutral text or box placeholders while content loads, then reveal children with isLoading=false. Match the pending content layout and provide one containing busy region and separate status announcement.
antipatterns: Do not add a Small Loader to content already represented by a skeleton.
Do not add undocumented shimmer, pulse, timings or annotation colors.
Do not leave pending interactive content mounted inside a placeholder.
Do not announce each placeholder or treat errors as endless loading.

components.name: IconButton
components.usage: Use for an icon-only action with a short accessible label. Choose the default or large icon while retaining the stable touch target.
antipatterns: Never omit the label or use a generic label unrelated to the action.
Do not introduce arbitrary icon sizes or unapproved icons.
Do not use a clickable div or add a filled background.

components.name: Link
components.usage: Use for inline navigation to a meaningful destination, preserving native anchor browser behavior. Typography is inherited and the underline always remains visible; external destinations stay in the same tab unless newTab is explicitly justified.

examples.label: Inline navigation
examples.code:
import { Link } from '@/design-system/{slug}';

Prüfen Sie Ihre Konten.

antipatterns: Never use Link for Save, Submit, Continue or Delete actions; use Button.
Do not use generic destination labels such as Hier klicken.
Do not force external links into new tabs automatically.
Do not remove the underline or add color variants.
Do not override wrapped-link line spacing: it reserves n4 underline thickness plus s10 clearance in every state to prevent hover overlap.
Do not stack links with bare line breaks or directly after a paragraph; use separate paragraphs with the canonical s40 spacing.
Do not duplicate destinations inside an already interactive container or conflict with row selection.
Do not introduce unexpected downloads or app switches without communicating the outcome.

components.name: ButtonSet
components.usage: Group closely related decisions with built-in responsive spacing and hierarchy. Choose buttons, links, icon-buttons or icon-links; use toolbar only for one named function requiring roving arrow-key focus.

examples.label: Named toolbar
examples.code: <ButtonSet type="icon-buttons" toolbar aria-label="Dokumentwerkzeuge"><IconButton icon="copy" label="Kopieren" onClick={copy} /><IconButton icon="edit" label="Bearbeiten" onClick={edit} /></ButtonSet>

antipatterns: Do not group independent actions or overload a decision group.
Never use more than one primary per set.
Secondary requires a primary unless there are exactly two equally weighted secondary buttons.
Do not use CSS ordering that disagrees with keyboard order.
Do not use toolbar without an accessible name or for unrelated functions.
Do not override built-in spacing or shrink the icon hit areas.

components.name: BarChart
components.usage: Use for up to seven horizontal CHF progress rows with ordered chart colors and optional signed percentage trends. Labels and unsigned amounts use default text; only signed changes use trend text colors. Provide a meaningful title; a hidden table mirrors every label, amount and trend.

examples.label: Account progress
examples.code: <BarChart title="Kontostände" max={2000} data={[{ label: 'Sparkonto', amount: 1234.5, trend: 3.7 }]} />

antipatterns: Never use danger in graphics; negatives use trend-negative.
Do not exceed seven series or manually reorder palette colors.
Do not hide visible values or remove the equivalent data table.
Do not add gridlines, rounded bars or shadows.

components.name: Legend
components.usage: Use alongside a chart with the same ordered data. Set withAmount to show CHF amounts beneath each label; omit it for a compact wrapping key. Labels and unsigned amounts use default text, not positive-trend green.
antipatterns: Do not use a different series order from the chart.
Do not exceed seven series or substitute arbitrary swatch colors.
Do not convey categories solely through color.

components.name: StockChart
components.usage: Use for a compact intraday quote card: instrument name, optional market, formatted value, signed percentage change and a line graph colored by the change's sign, with optional dashed reference value and end dot. Hovering the line shows the point's time and value in a Popover-styled tooltip. A hidden table mirrors every time and value.

examples.label: Index card
examples.code: <StockChart name="DAX" market="Schweiz" value="0.9606" change={0.11} date="26.08.2025" data={quotes} reference={previousClose} ticks={['08:00','12:00','18:00']} />

antipatterns: Never use danger for the line; negatives use trend-negative.
Do not pass custom line colors; the sign of change decides.
Do not add gridlines, area fills, shadows or animations.
Do not show the change without its sign.

components.name: Snackbar
components.usage: Use for brief, non-blocking outcomes with a polite text announcement and optional dismissal. The application owns visibility and placement.
antipatterns: Do not use for blocking or critical decisions.
Do not put action controls in the announcement or invent expiry durations.

components.name: Tooltip
components.usage: Use for supplementary non-interactive text available on hover and keyboard focus; supply an accessible ref-forwarding trigger.
antipatterns: Never put interactive content or essential instructions inside.
Never use a tooltip as the only accessible label.

components.name: Popover
components.usage: Use for named supplementary content anchored to a control, with keyboard focus, dismissal and restoration managed by Radix.
antipatterns: Do not omit the dialog label.
Do not use for blocking decisions or arbitrary visual variants.

components.name: Toast
components.usage: Use the selected inverse notification for richer non-blocking feedback. Keep priority order at every viewport: Secondary before tertiary Link in DOM, visual and Tab order. On XS, stack the full-width Secondary above the centered Link with s40 spacing; from SM upward, use a left-aligned horizontal wrapping row with vertically centered controls and s40 spacing.

examples.label: Typical usage
examples.code: <Toast title="Zahlung eingerichtet" actions={<Button inverted variant="secondary" onClick={acknowledge}>OK</Button>}>Ab morgen wird automatisch investiert.</Toast>

antipatterns: Never place Primary on the inverse surface.
Do not steal focus or invent timed dismissal.
Do not substitute arbitrary icons, colors or rounded buttons.
Never reverse priority on mobile: Secondary precedes tertiary Link at every viewport, with matching visual and Tab order.

components.name: Alert
components.usage: Use info, success, warning or danger in-page messages on bg-page with the matching semantic n4 border and standard-bold title. Title/body are independently optional; action composes a link-style Button and iconAction a named IconButton.

examples.label: Save outcome
examples.code: <Alert variant="success" title="Änderungen gespeichert">Ihre Kontoeinstellungen wurden aktualisiert.</Alert>

examples.label: Error recovery
examples.code: <Alert variant="warning" title="Bitte prüfen Sie Ihre Angaben" action={<Button variant="link" onClick={retry}>Erneut versuchen</Button>}>Bitte prüfen Sie Ihre Angaben.</Alert>

antipatterns: Never use trend-negative instead of UI danger.
Do not tint the white master surface or body text, add decorative severity icons or shadows, or assume the optional icon control means dismissal.
Do not move focus or automatically dismiss important feedback.
Do not convey status through color alone.

components.name: Table
components.usage: Use for native non-stacked tabular data with an accessible label and keyboard-scrollable overflow.
antipatterns: Do not turn the table into independently rendered columns or clickable rows.

components.name: TableHeader
components.usage: Group native column-heading rows.
antipatterns: Do not use ordinary cells instead of column headings.

components.name: TableBody
components.usage: Group the native data rows.
antipatterns: Do not put div elements directly inside table sections.

components.name: TableFooter
components.usage: Use an optional native footer for summary rows.
antipatterns: Do not invent footer color treatments.

components.name: TableRow
components.usage: Compose one native data or heading row.
antipatterns: Do not make the row a substitute button or link.

components.name: TableHead
components.usage: Use native scope-aware headings; alignment is left, right or center.
antipatterns: Do not omit accessible headings for action columns.

components.name: TableCell
components.usage: Use text, numeric or actions cells. Numeric defaults right and actions preserve existing IconButton targets.
antipatterns: Do not use bare clickable icons, custom colors or curved amount separators.

components.name: Accordion
components.usage: Group expandable content in the selected responsive Figma width. Single is collapsible by default; multiple supports independent panels. Controlled and initial values are arrays.

examples.label: FAQ
examples.code: <Accordion defaultValue={['cost']}><AccordionItem value='cost'><AccordionTrigger>Kartenkosten</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>Die Kosten hängen von der Karte ab.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem></Accordion>

antipatterns: Do not narrow the root twice inside a pre-narrowed column.
Do not add undocumented animation or card styling.

components.name: AccordionItem
components.usage: Compose one uniquely identified expandable section inside Accordion.
antipatterns: Never reuse an item value in the same root.
Do not put items outside Accordion.

components.name: AccordionTrigger
components.usage: Use a descriptive full-width native header button with a decorative chevron. Set headingLevel to match the document hierarchy.
antipatterns: Do not nest links or buttons in the trigger.
Never leave the trigger label empty.

components.name: AccordionContent
components.usage: Place explanatory content and real navigation within the associated panel. Closed content is removed from keyboard navigation.
antipatterns: Do not force hidden interactive content to remain focusable.
Do not remove the token-backed content insets.
